result:
I'm done: **final.py scores 0.5788 on the search split, up from 0.365 for the LRU baseline. I used 8 of the 24 scorer calls.** It's valid and runs well within the time limit. I followed the evolve skill under its default budget (about 15 minutes, 24 calls). I stopped after about 9 minutes because the last several ideas made no measurable difference.

The skill also asks for a held-out check, but `./score` only scores the search split. So the held-out numbers below come from my own trace generator, run on seeds I never tuned on. Treat them as a sanity check, not as the final score.

| | Search score (official) | Held-out (my local traces) |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (LRU) | 0.365 | 0.293 |
| First good answer (TinyLFU) | 0.522 | 0.469 |
| Best single policy (LIRS) | 0.564 | 0.492 |
| **Final (final.py)** | **0.579** | **0.518** |

**Why it's better:** each known eviction policy wins on some trace types and loses on others. TinyLFU is best on hot keys, ARC on recency, and LIRS on loops and scans. So final.py runs all three side by side, tracking only which keys each would hold. It keeps a running hit count for each one, with older hits counting less. The real cache evicts whatever the current leader just evicted, so on each trace it does about as well as the best of the three would. The TinyLFU copy forgets old popularity more slowly than usual (it halves counts every 20× capacity requests instead of 10×), because ARC already covers fast-changing patterns. Per-trace results on the scorer: hot_with_scans 0.249, loop_and_hot 0.636, phases 0.646, mixed 0.272, recency 0.847, shifting_loops 0.824.

**Approaches tried and dropped:**
- **ARC and S3-FIFO alone:** strong on recency, weak on loops (S3-FIFO scored 0.453).
- **TinyLFU with a self-adjusting front-section size:** 0.525. It gained on recency but lost on loops.
- **LIRS with a self-adjusting size:** no gain.
- **Adding a fourth policy** (S3-FIFO, a second LIRS or TinyLFU, hyperbolic caching, or SIEVE): no gain.
- **Voting on evictions across the policies:** no gain.
- **Tuning how quickly the leader switches:** made no difference.

**Scorer log (search split):**

| Candidate | Score | Kept? |
|---|---|---|
| c_tlfu | 0.5219 | First champion |
| c_s3 | 0.4525 | Dropped |
| c_atlfu2 | 0.5255 | Superseded |
| c_lirs2 | 0.5644 | Superseded |
| c_ens (LIRS + TinyLFU + S3-FIFO) | 0.5691 | Superseded |
| c_ens3 (ARC + TinyLFU + LIRS) | 0.5767 | Superseded |
| c_ens5 (slower-forgetting TinyLFU) | 0.5788 | Final pick |
| final.py (c_ens5 without the unused S3-FIFO code) | 0.5788 | Confirm run |

**Weak spots:** hot_with_scans and mixed stay around 0.25 to 0.27 for every policy I tried. On loop_and_hot the ensemble scores 0.636, while TinyLFU on its own got 0.655. The likely cause is the ensemble switching leaders back and forth on that trace. Slowing the switching didn't help on my local traces, so I didn't spend scorer calls chasing it.

All candidates and the local test scripts (`harness.py`, `sweep.py`, `opt.py`) are in the task folder.
